reply_text:
㊥ (`"we need the features we are building, and not just for me"`) Yes. The claude-6 case is exactly what the ledger is for, and today it can't see it. 象 only reads turns typed into a REPL: 727 since 3 October, plus 6 from Matrix. Bells between agents aren't recorded at all. So the path your request took (claude-2, then claude-4, then folded into codex-23's packet) has no acts and no open ports, and nothing can notice that half of it was never answered. To catch it, bells have to become turns in the ledger: a request opens a port, the completion bell answers it, and a relayed request stays linked to the one it came from.

🈖 (how the claude-6 case would look with that in place)
- **Your endorsement.** Your endorsement of the idea is an act in claude-6's session.
- **claude-2's bell to claude-4.** It relays the idea and opens a port in claude-4's ledger, linked back to your act. The link exists if the bell quotes your words in a bracket, which is the same mechanism I built today for replies.
- **claude-4 folds it into codex-23's packet.** That opens a second port, linked to the first.
- **codex-23's answer.** It covers the reload question only. The capture question stays open on claude-4's port, and therefore on yours.
- **The reminder machine.** It nudges whoever holds the oldest open link, here claude-4, instead of you finding out weeks later.

㊭ (order of work)
1. **Record every bell and whistle as a turn** of the caller–recipient pair, with the completion bell as its reply. The pair's turns get the same acts and ports as REPL turns. I'd first make a discovery pass: where in Agency to hook it, how many bells a day there are, and what reading them with 象 would cost. Then build it.
2. **Mark bells with the proforma.** At present CLAUDE.md says bells are not marked. Asking for one mark per request, with your quoted words in the bracket when relaying something you said, makes each request a separate act. So "two questions in one packet" becomes two ports instead of one. This changes CLAUDE.md, so it's your decision.
3. **Follow links across sessions.** The kernel today only makes agreements within one agent's session. A relayed request needs its port to stay open until the request it was relayed into closes.
4. **Rerun the demo**, extended so that claude-5 bells a second agent with half of a two-part request. The check: the unanswered half shows as open in both ledgers, and the reminder machine nudges the agent holding it.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I start on step 1's discovery pass now, and add the step-2 line to CLAUDE.md, saying that bells carry one mark per request and quote the operator's words when relaying them? The three-turn retest of today's fixes can wait until step 1 is built, and then be folded into the extended demo.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what changed)
1. **The session id.** A first turn recorded under the placeholder session ("claude-5 (awaiting session)") now takes the agent's real session when the reply ends. Its offers are then in the same session as your answer, so accepting one creates the obligation.
2. **A pointer at a question answers the question.** "🈯: yes, call it elephant.txt" now answers the 🈯 question and closes it. Before, it was taken as accepting the offer next to it, so that offer was accepted twice. This reverses a rule claude-2 and I settled earlier today: when your pointer names something other than an offer, your "yes" answers that thing, not whichever offer came last.
3. **Your requests can now close.** When an agent's reply quotes your words in its bracket, e.g. `㊢ ("do it in a new git repo at /tmp/xiang-demo, with a commit")`, that reply answers the part of your turn holding those words. On the demo records, this closes "do it in a new git repo…" in turn 2 and the request for two questions in turn 1.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(`"we have the 小象 parse to go on right away"`) Ports are still computed from 象's reading, not 小象's, for now.
- **What happened in the demo.** 小象's draft of your turn 2 took "🈯:" and "🈸:" as your own clarify. In this notation they are pointers answering the agent, so both of its fragments were the wrong kind. Using that draft would have opened wrong ports for the minute before 象 corrected it.
- **What the delay is.** The quote match itself only needs your words, so the remaining wait is 象's reading, about 1–2 minutes per turn.
- **What would make it immediate.** Teach 小象 that a mark followed by a colon is a pointer, then let ports use its draft. That's a separate fix, and I can do it next if you want ports to update immediately.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (what I checked) Each fix has a test built from the three demo records. With each fix disabled in turn, 12 assertions fail. With all three in, the turn-acts, reply-target, turn-service and tangle tests together give 76 tests and 365 assertions, 0 failures. Two of earlier today's tests pinned the reversed rule and now expect the new behaviour. After the reload, the routes probe answered 200.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(expected this time)
- **After turn 2:**
  - both questions close;
  - there is one acceptance (option 1), with an obligation on the agent to you;
  - your "do it in a new git repo…" request closes, if the agent quotes it in its bracket.
- **After turn 3:** only the new 🈸 question stays open, plus your "Don't do anything yet" and "and then stop". Those two are constraints: they stay in force until withdrawn and are never closed by an answer.
- **Not expected to work:** the commit linking to the offer, because commits in a /tmp repo still aren't captured.
